speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a psychiatric condition and a new onset movement disorder; to help me understand what is happening, can you describe the specific movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context. Given your recent start on risperidone and the new onset of movement issues, have you noticed any stiffness, tremors, or repetitive movements like writhing or facial masking since beginning the medication?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Risperidone-induced Acute Dystonia/Extrapyramidal Symptoms (specifically Akathisia). The patient's description of an "inability to remain still," restlessness, fidgeting, and leg crossing/uncrossing is classic for akathisia, a common side effect of high-potency first-generation antipsychotics like risperidone. This diagnosis is based on the clinical presentation following the initiation of the medication two months ago.
